_README: Where the A.T. meets water, and which shelters and campsites have water
they can actually walk to (#529).
GENERATED by build_trail_water.py - re-run that script rather than
editing rows here, and review the diff it produces.
`crossings` are exact geometric intersections of ATC's centerline with
OSM stream and river ways: the two lines cross, so a hiker walking the trail
walks through the water. export_poi.py publishes them as the `crossing`
poi_type, which has been declared and empty since it was declared.
`sites` carries one record per shelter and campsite. A record publishes
water only when a hiker could reach it - within 100 ft AND under a 35%
grade, measured from real USGS elevations at both ends, because a stream
90 ft away and 120 ft below is not a water source however close the map
says it is. Everything rejected keeps its numbers and its reason, so
widening either gate is a decision somebody can make from this file.
A published water point is a real coordinate on the stream (the nearest
point on the reach, not a vertex), so lib/poi_sites.py's 60 m proximity
fold attaches it to the site with no second matching rule.
Streams come from the Geofabrik state extracts this pipeline already
downloads, so the derivation runs offline (ODbL - attribution rides on
every published description). Only the two elevations behind the grade
gate come from USGS 3DEP, and they reach no published field.

source.title: OpenStreetMap stream and river ways (Geofabrik state extracts) + USGS 3DEP point elevations
source.licence: OSM is ODbL - attribution and share-alike, the terms the basemap and fetch_osm_water.py already comply with; every published description carries 'Mapped by OpenStreetMap contributors'. The two elevations behind the grade gate come from USGS 3DEP (public domain) and reach no published field.
